title: Leonida Legend
note: Trophy names, grades and official descriptions are verbatim from the official list. Guide text, phases, difficulty and time estimates are this guide's own work.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: There is no shortcut: this trophy pops the moment the other 54 are yours. Treat it as the receipt for the whole hunt, not a task of its own. Work the phases in the order the roadmap gives — story first, then strangers and activities, exploration and combat, partner play, and the slow counters last — and this will land on its own. The only real advice is bookkeeping: keep the checklist honest, tick trophies the day you earn them, and never trust memory for a counter you can check in a menu.
trophies.tips: It pops automatically — your job is finishing the other 54, not chasing this one.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; the platinum itself

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy most players will earn. Follow the opening beats: meet the cast, learn the basic controls, and let the mission carry you to its end. There is nothing to prepare and nothing to miss — just play the story from the start and the trophy unlocks when the mission's closing scene plays. If you skipped the opening once, replaying Gone Fishing from the mission menu counts too.
trophies.tips: Unmissable: it is the opening mission, so simply start the story.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Chapter 1 is the first full stretch of the campaign, and this trophy is its finishing line. Play the chapter's missions in order — the story gates progress, so there is no way to skip ahead or fall behind. Expect a mix of driving, on-foot action and cutscenes that introduce Vice City and the people you will be working for. When the chapter's final mission ends and the next chapter card appears, the trophy pops. Nothing here needs a special approach: keep playing.
trophies.tips: Story-gated — progress through the missions and it arrives on its own.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Chapter 2 raises the stakes and the heat: more moving parts, bigger jobs, and the first real sense of how the campaign's crews and rivalries fit together. Work through the chapter's mission chain in order, using the time between missions to restock ammo and keep a decent car handy — a fast, sturdy ride saves more time than any shortcut. The trophy unlocks when the chapter's closing mission ends. As with every story trophy, it cannot be missed; replaying missions is always an option.
trophies.tips: Keep a fast car and full ammo between missions; the chapter does the rest.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: By Chapter 3 you are properly in Vice City, and this trophy marks the end of that stretch of the story. Expect the missions to lean harder on planning: read each briefing, pick the approach that fits your loadout, and use cover rather than sprinting through open ground. The chapter's final mission is the gate — finish it and the trophy unlocks. If a mission gives you trouble, the retry checkpoint is generous; failing a mission never costs progress toward this trophy.
trophies.tips: Read each briefing and fight from cover; retries never cost you the trophy.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is where the campaign starts paying off its setup, and this trophy is the reward for seeing it through. The missions here tend to be longer and to chain several objectives, so keep an eye on the objective line and save a solid weapon loadout for the finales. Finish the chapter's last mission and the trophy pops as the next chapter opens. There is no optional objective to worry about — completion of the mission chain is the whole requirement.
trophies.tips: Long chained missions: watch the objective line and save your best weapons for the end.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The final mission is the campaign's last word, and this gold trophy is its prize. You will only reach it after the full story, so arrive prepared: a full weapon wheel, body armour, and a fast escape vehicle parked somewhere sensible. The mission itself is a multi-stage finale — expect set-pieces, a long firefight, and a closing choice or chase. Take it slowly, use checkpoints, and let the mission's own pacing carry you. When the credits roll, the gold is yours.
trophies.tips: Arrive with full armour and a fast getaway car; use the checkpoints, don't rush the finale.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a story mission, and this trophy is simply its completion. It sits early enough that you will meet it naturally while playing the campaign — no special preparation, no optional objective, no route to take. Just start the mission from its marker when it appears, follow the objectives, and finish it. The trophy pops at the mission's end screen. Like all story trophies, it can be replayed from the mission list if you ever need to.
trophies.tips: Story mission — it arrives on its own as you play the campaign.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is one of the campaign's big set-pieces, and this trophy marks the day you pull it off. Heists in this series reward preparation more than reflexes: before you start, stock up on ammo and armour, and pick a getaway vehicle you can actually drive under pressure. During the job, follow the plan the mission lays out — the scripted beats do the heavy lifting — and keep moving when the alarm goes up. Finish the heist and the trophy unlocks at the end screen.
trophies.tips: Stock ammo and armour first, and have a getaway car ready before you trigger the job.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a story mission, and completing it is all this trophy asks. It will appear on your map as the campaign reaches it — head to the marker, watch the setup play out, and work through the mission's objectives in order. Expect a mix of driving and on-foot sections with a few scripted turns; nothing in it demands a particular loadout. The trophy unlocks when the mission completes. If you fail a section, the checkpoint drops you back in close by.
trophies.tips: Follow the objectives in order; checkpoints are close if a section goes wrong.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is a story mission with a show-business edge, and this trophy is its completion. The mission will unlock on the map as the campaign progresses — go to its marker and play through the sequence. Expect the mission to mix social set-up with a harder second half, so keep a weapon handy even when the opening feels calm. Work the objectives in order and the trophy pops at the end screen. Like every story trophy, it can be replayed later if needed.
trophies.tips: Keep a weapon ready even when the opening feels calm — the second half bites.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown takes you into Vice City International Airport for a story mission, and finishing it earns this trophy. The mission appears as the campaign reaches the airport arc — follow its marker, work the objectives, and expect tight corridors and close-quarters fighting inside the terminal areas. Bring a close-range weapon and plenty of ammo, and use cover at the chokepoints rather than pushing through them. Complete the mission and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.tips: Bring a close-range weapon for the terminal corridors and fight from cover.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is a late-campaign story mission, and this trophy marks its completion. By this point the campaign expects you to be comfortable with the full toolkit: driving, shooting from cover, and switching weapons on the move. The mission is a long one with several stages, so pace yourself, use the checkpoints, and restock at any lull the mission gives you. Finish the final stage and the trophy pops. It is story-gated, so it cannot be missed.
trophies.tips: A long multi-stage mission: use checkpoints and restock at every lull.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: 100% completion is the long checklist the game itself keeps: every story mission, every stranger strand, every activity, every collectible set, every stunt jump, every hidden package of progress the world holds. Open the in-game stats or checklist screen and work through it category by category — the roadmap on this page follows the same order for a reason. The last few percent are always the grind: stunts, card sets, WAiNK spots, challenges. When the counter hits 100%, this gold trophy pops — and the platinum follows.
trophies.tips: Use the in-game 100% checklist and clear it category by category; the grind is the last 10%.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Stunts are the game's jump-and-airtime challenges, scattered across Leonida wherever a ramp, a hill or a rooftop edge invites a fast car to fly. You need 250 of them, so this is a volume trophy: make stunting a habit, not a session. Keep a fast car, hit every ramp you pass, and let the counter climb as you travel. The in-game stats screen tracks your total, so check it between phases and mop up the remainder late — ramps near the city are the easiest to repeat, and a stunt you land while travelling to another trophy still counts.
trophies.tips: Stunt as you travel: hit every ramp you pass and the counter climbs on its own.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Leonida is full of pastimes — the shooting range, drone races, fishing, the arcade, bowling, races of every kind — and this trophy asks you to try each type once. It is a sampler, not a mastery test: find one of each activity, play a single round, and move on. Use the map's activity icons to find what you have not tried yet, and do this early, while the story is still opening the map — it also points you at the activities other trophies will ask you to master later.
trophies.tips: Do it early: the map's activity icons show what you haven't tried yet.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The Shooting Range runs a set of timed target challenges, and this silver trophy wants a gold medal in every one of them. Each challenge scores accuracy, speed and target priority, so the trick is not spraying: line up shots, lead moving targets slightly, and reload during the gaps between waves. Visit the range between missions to learn the layouts, then chase golds one challenge at a time — the easiest first, to learn the scoring. A steady hand beats a fast trigger here.
trophies.tips: Aim, don't spray: lead moving targets and reload between waves; easiest challenge first.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; shooting range challenges

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun runs drone races at several courses around Leonida, and this trophy needs a win at every location. Each course has its own shape — tight gates, open straights, altitude changes — so learn a course before racing it for real: fly a practice lap, note where the gates turn, and keep the drone low through the tight sections. Win one race per location and the trophy pops. If a course keeps beating you, switch drones: handling differs more than speed does.
trophies.tips: Fly a practice lap first, keep low through tight gates, and try a different drone if stuck.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; Top Fun drone races

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Twenty different race wins is a breadth test: street races, off-road, water, air — whatever the game counts as a race type, you need a win in twenty of them. The fastest route is variety: take every race you pass, race each type once, and do not repeat a won race when a new one is on the map. A tuned car helps, but clean lines help more — brake early, cut the corner, and let rivals make the mistakes. The in-game race list shows which types you have won.
trophies.tips: Race each type once and never repeat a won race; the race list shows what is left.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal is the fishing rival, and this trophy is a straight contest: beat him in a fishing challenge. Fishing here is a timing game — cast where the water moves, watch the line, and reel in steady bursts instead of holding the button down. Cal's score is the bar; play a few rounds to learn the rhythm of the bites, then fish the challenge for real. Pick a quiet spot, take your time, and remember that a patient retrieve out-scores a frantic one.
trophies.tips: Reel in steady bursts, don't hold the button; learn the bite rhythm in practice rounds.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: The arcade is Leonida's noisiest corner, and this trophy asks for one completed game — any cabinet, any game. Walk in, pick a machine, and play it to its end: some games are a single high-score run, others a short level or a timed round. The trophy pops when the game's own end screen appears, win or lose, so there is no skill gate here at all. If the first cabinet confuses you, try another; the arcade's whole point is variety, and the cheapest game in the room counts just as much as the hardest.
trophies.tips: Any cabinet counts — pick the simplest game and play it to its end screen.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy is one of the strangers whose missions arrive in stages, and this trophy is the end of his strand. Stranger missions unlock one at a time: finish one, let some in-game time pass, and watch for Andy's next marker to appear. His final mission is the one that counts, and it will be marked like the rest. If a marker goes quiet for a while, sleep or play other content and check back — the strand advances on the game's own schedule, not yours. Finish the last mission and the trophy pops.
trophies.tips: Strands advance in stages — if a marker goes quiet, let in-game days pass and check back.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; stranger mission strand

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton's strand works the same way as every stranger's: a chain of missions that appears one step at a time, with gaps while the game waits for the right moment. Take each mission as its marker appears, and between steps do other work — the strand will not hurry for you. His final mission closes the chain and earns this trophy. Keep an eye on the map for his icon after each step, and if nothing shows, advance the in-game clock by sleeping or playing elsewhere.
trophies.tips: Take missions as markers appear; sleep or play elsewhere when the strand pauses.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; stranger mission strand

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's strand is another staged chain of stranger missions, ending in a final mission that earns this trophy. The pattern is familiar by now: accept a mission from its marker, complete it, then wait for the next one to surface — sometimes after an in-game day or two. Do not camp on the spot; play the rest of the game and the marker will come back. Finish Billy's last mission and the trophy pops at its end screen.
trophies.tips: Don't camp the marker — play other content and the next step will surface.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; stranger mission strand

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Strangers & Freaks is the big stranger trophy: eight complete mission strands across Leonida. Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone are five of them; the remaining three are other strangers you will meet as you explore. Each strand is a staged chain — take missions as their markers appear, let in-game time pass between steps, and finish each strand's final mission. The counter ticks per finished strand, so check the stats screen to see which ones remain. It is a patience trophy, not a skill one.
trophies.tips: Finish whole strands, not single missions; the stats screen shows which strands remain.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; stranger mission strands

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's strand is a staged chain of stranger missions, and its final mission earns this trophy. Accept each mission from its marker, complete it, and wait for the next step — the gaps between steps are part of the design, so use them for other trophies. Randy's missions lean on the stranger side of Leonida: odd jobs, odd people, and a payoff that only makes sense at the end of the chain. Finish his last mission and the trophy pops.
trophies.tips: Use the gaps between strand steps for other trophies; the chain finishes on its own schedule.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; stranger mission strand

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone's strand closes with a final mission, and completing it earns this trophy. Like the other stranger chains, it arrives in stages: a mission marker, a job, a pause, then the next marker. Follow the chain to its end and the trophy pops at the final mission's end screen. If you are working several strands at once — which the roadmap recommends — Tyrone's markers will interleave with the others, and the Strangers & Freaks counter will tick along with them.
trophies.tips: Run strands in parallel — markers interleave and the big stranger trophy ticks along.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; stranger mission strand

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditation spots are quiet corners scattered across Leonida — clifftops, beaches, wetlands, anywhere the view does the talking. This trophy wants you to meditate at every one of them. The spots are marked once you are near, so the work is travel: sweep the map region by region, sit at each spot, and let the meditation play out. A few spots only reveal themselves after you have explored their area, so finish the exploration phase first and the last spots will already be on your map.
trophies.tips: Sweep region by region after exploring; spots reveal themselves once you're near.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret wants a unique animal hunted, and this trophy is the proof. Unique animals are one-of-a-kind creatures tied to specific corners of Leonida — the hunt is about finding the right place and the right moment, not about firepower. Take the hunt seriously: bring a scoped rifle, move slowly, and watch for tracks or calls that mark the animal's ground. One clean, patient hunt is all it takes; rushing it just scares the quarry off. Check Bret's strand for the opening clue.
trophies.tips: Scoped rifle, slow approach, watch for tracks — one patient hunt is all it takes.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; unique animal hunt

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Collectible cards come in sets, and this silver trophy needs three complete sets. Cards are tucked into shops, hideouts, mission areas and quiet corners all over Leonida — the hunt is mostly thoroughness. Pick up every card you pass from the start, keep a checklist of which sets are close to done, and use the map's collectible hints in the late game to find the stragglers. Three full sets is the line; the rest of the sets are for 100% completion. A set you finish early is progress you never repeat.
trophies.tips: Grab every card from the start; finish three sets and the late-game hints find the rest.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; collectible card sets

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It is the game's tagging or photo-spot system, and this silver trophy wants it done at 100 locations across Leonida. The count is the challenge, not any single spot: treat it as a travel habit. Whenever you enter a new area, look for the WAiNK prompt, do it, and move on. The in-game counter tracks your total, so check it between regions and sweep the thin spots last — the city's dense districts fill fast, while the wetlands and highways take a deliberate pass.
trophies.tips: WAiNK everywhere you go; dense districts fill fast, wetlands need a deliberate sweep.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Challenges are the game's side objectives — the small tasks layered over missions, activities and exploration — and this trophy needs 50 of them completed. The fastest route is to let them accumulate: play the story, try every activity, and check the challenges menu often so you know what is close. Some challenges complete themselves while you play; others need a deliberate detour, like a specific stunt or a weapon type. Fifty is a milestone on the way to the full set, so do not grind it early — let it arrive.
trophies.tips: Check the challenges menu often and let 50 accumulate naturally — don't grind it early.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: This one needs both protagonists together: build a four-star wanted level with your partner beside you, then lose the heat and escape. The partner is the key — the trophy only counts when you are playing as a pair, so start the attempt from a partner activity or a co-op moment. Once the stars hit four, break line of sight, switch to a fast car, and run the heat off the old-fashioned way: alleys, tunnels, and distance. When the stars clear with your partner still with you, the trophy pops.
trophies.tips: Only counts as a pair — start from a partner moment, then break line of sight and run.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; partner wanted level

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Three shops, back to back, with your partner, without ever losing your wanted level — that is the chain this trophy wants. The trick is the route: pick three small shops close together, plan the order before you start, and keep the getaways short. Rob the first, move immediately to the second while the heat is still low, then the third — and do not stop to fight. If the wanted level clears between shops, the chain breaks and you start over. A fast car parked between shops is worth more than a big gun.
trophies.tips: Three small shops close together, planned route, never stop to fight — a break resets the chain.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; partner shop robberies

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discovering a vehicle means sitting in it — or at least getting close enough for the game to log it — and this trophy wants 100 different ones. Leonida's traffic is the catalogue: city streets give you the common cars fast, while the rare ones hide in mission areas, wealthy districts, and the countryside. Make it a habit to hop into anything unfamiliar you pass, and check the stats screen for your count. The last dozen are the hunt; mission vehicles and parked rarities fill the gaps.
trophies.tips: Hop into anything unfamiliar you pass; mission vehicles fill the last dozen.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; vehicle discovery counter

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus is the slow-motion aim mode, and this trophy wants five takedowns inside a single use of it. The setup matters more than the aim: find a spot with five enemies close together — a gang hideout or a mission firefight with a cluster — then trigger Combat Focus and work the group methodically, one target at a time, before the meter runs out. A high-capacity weapon helps, but the real trick is picking the right fight. If the group scatters, reset and try a denser spot.
trophies.tips: Pick a dense group first — a gang hideout — then trigger Focus and work it methodically.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: An unscheduled departure at VCIA means leaving the airport in a way the airport did not plan — on foot through a fence, in a stolen vehicle through a gate, or by any route that is not the front door. The trophy is about improvisation: get into the airport grounds, then leave by a route the game treats as an exit it did not schedule. The simplest read is to drive out through a service gate or fence line while the game is tracking your position. Once you are clear of the grounds by an unscheduled route, it pops.
trophies.tips: Leave VCIA by a service gate or fence line, not the front door.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Rhinos are the tanks of Leonida, and this trophy is about spending time in one — hot, loud, and very hard to stop. Get into a Rhino, then enjoy it: roll through the streets, shrug off the traffic, and let the wanted level climb while you stay inside the armour. The exact trigger is spending time in the tank under pressure, so do not park it and walk away — drive it, use it, and let the heat come to you. Military areas are the obvious place to find one; a wanted level is the obvious way to keep it interesting.
trophies.tips: Stay in the tank and drive it under pressure — parking it doesn't count.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: A jewellery store, robbed without being detected, is a stealth job — and this trophy is the quiet version of the loud heists elsewhere on the list. Plan it like a burglary: case the store first, learn the camera and guard pattern, and enter when the floor is clear. Move slowly, take the goods without tripping an alarm, and leave before anyone knows you were there. If you are spotted, the attempt fails — abort, lose the heat, and try again. Patience is the whole skill here.
trophies.tips: Case it first, learn the guard pattern, and abort the moment you're spotted.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Bank vaults are the big scores, and this silver trophy wants five of them robbed — and escaped from. Each vault is a full job: get in, crack or breach the vault, grab the take, and then get clear of the response. The escape is half the trophy, so plan it before you go in: a fast car, a route away from the heat, and no stopping to fight. Five vaults, five clean escapes. Do them one at a time between other work, and keep the take for the spending trophies later.
trophies.tips: Plan the escape before you go in — five vaults, five clean getaways, one at a time.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; bank vault robberies

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: An armoured truck is a moving vault, and this trophy is the classic intercept: stop the truck, get the crew out or the doors open, take the cash, and escape before the response arrives. The intercept itself is the easy part — a roadblock or a well-timed ram — but the escape is where attempts fail, so have your getaway ready before you strike. Pick a quiet stretch of road, hit the truck fast, and be gone before the wanted level climbs past what you can outrun. One clean job is all it takes.
trophies.tips: Hit it on a quiet road with the getaway ready — the escape is where attempts fail.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; armoured truck robbery

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida means exactly that: every region of the map, from Vice City's neon streets to the wetlands, the keys, and the far highways. The game tracks fog-of-war or area discovery, so the work is travel — drive the map edge to edge, take the roads you have never taken, and let the counter climb. A helicopter or a fast boat opens the awkward corners. Check the map screen for the grey patches that remain, and finish them in one deliberate sweep after the story is done.
trophies.tips: Drive edge to edge, then sweep the grey patches on the map in one deliberate pass.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Every gang in Leonida runs illegal operations, and this trophy wants one robbed from each of them. The work is identification: learn which gang holds which operation — the game marks them once you are close — then hit each one and get clear. The operations differ in layout and resistance, so do not treat them as identical; case each one, bring the right loadout, and escape cleanly. The counter ticks per gang, so the stats screen shows which gangs are left.
trophies.tips: One operation per gang — case each layout first; the stats screen shows gangs left.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Ocean Beach is Vice City's postcard, and this trophy is a quiet moment on it: find a bar or spot with a view over the water, order a cocktail, and enjoy it. There is no skill here and no rush — the trophy is the game's way of asking you to stop and look at the place. Walk the beachfront until a venue offers the prompt, sit down, and let the scene play. It is the easiest trophy on the list and one of the nicest; do it early, when the city is still new.
trophies.tips: Walk the beachfront until a venue offers the prompt — do it early, while the city is new.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: A vehicle showroom, smashed your way out of, in classic style — this trophy is pure chaos with a wink. The idea is the old-school escape: get inside a showroom, make a mess, and drive straight out through the glass in a display car. The game rewards the spectacle, so commit to it: pick a fast car on the floor, aim for the front, and do not brake. If the attempt fizzles, walk out, lose any heat, and try another showroom. One good smash is all it takes.
trophies.tips: Pick a fast display car, aim for the front glass, and don't brake.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Kolt & Associates runs a bowling alley, and this trophy is about the follow-through — finishing a game there properly. Bowling in this series is a timing mini-game: line up the shot, judge the power, and release cleanly. Play a full game, frame by frame, and the trophy pops at the end of it. It does not ask for a high score or a strike, just a completed game with the follow-through the description calls out. A quiet evening's diversion that also counts toward the activities sampler.
trophies.tips: Play a full game frame by frame — no score needed, just finish it.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal is the payoff of the two-protagonist system: a job or moment where the pair's combined presence draws a crowd, a payout, or a reputation boost. The trigger is a partner activity done well — the game measures how the pair performs together, not either one alone. Look for partner moments on the map, take them with both protagonists, and play them cleanly. When the partnership's appeal lands — the crowd, the payout, the reaction — the trophy pops.
trophies.tips: Take partner moments with both protagonists and play them cleanly — the pair is judged together.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Choices made, for better or worse — this trophy is the story's way of marking a decision point. Somewhere in the campaign a choice will present itself, and this trophy records that you made it. There is no right answer to find and no preparation to do: play the story, and when a decision arrives, choose. The trophy pops on the choice itself, not on its outcome, so do not agonise over it — pick the option that fits your run and keep playing. The story continues either way.
trophies.tips: No right answer — when a story choice arrives, just choose and keep playing.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm — this trophy is about a retry. Somewhere in the game there is a task, a jump, a shot or a stunt that is meant to be attempted more than once, and the trophy pops on the successful second try. The honest way to earn it is to keep playing and let it happen: fail something, try again, and succeed. If you are chasing it deliberately, pick a repeatable challenge — a stunt, a race, a range target — and treat the first attempt as the warm-up. The second one counts.
trophies.tips: Fail something, try again, succeed — a repeatable challenge is the cleanest route.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? — this trophy is the game's nod to its strangest corner: an event, a sighting, or an encounter that does not fit the rest of Leonida. The trigger is finding it, and finding it means exploring the odd places after dark — the wetlands, the empty highways, the corners of the map where the game hides its jokes. Keep an eye out while you sweep the map for exploration, and when something genuinely weird happens, the trophy pops. It is a discovery, not a task.
trophies.tips: Explore the odd corners after dark while sweeping the map — it's a discovery, not a task.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: A melee drive-by is exactly what it sounds like: striking a target with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle — and this trophy wants ten pins, bowling style. The setup is the hard part: a slow vehicle, a clear stretch with pedestrians or targets, and a melee weapon with reach. Drive past at low speed, swing as you pass, and keep the run going. It is deliberately silly and deliberately hard to do cleanly, so expect a few attempts. A quiet street and a patient driver beat a fast car here.
trophies.tips: Slow vehicle, clear stretch, swing as you pass — patience beats speed here.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills are dirty money, and laundering them through your contacts turns them clean — this trophy wants $250,000 of it washed. The loop is the economy itself: earn marked bills from jobs, pass them to a contact, and take the clean cut. The amount is the grind, so launder steadily from the start instead of hoarding bills for one big session, and watch the cut: contacts take their share, so the bills you feed in are always more than the clean total. Keep a contact in mind after every paying job, and the counter will climb on its own. The clean money then funds the spending trophy too.
trophies.tips: Launder after every paying job from the start — hoarding bills for one session wastes time.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops and this trophy is yours. It is the economy's other half: everything you buy — clothes, weapons, ammo, food, cars, upgrades — counts toward the same total. The honest route is to spend as you play, not to save and splurge: buy the gear the other trophies need, upgrade the cars you actually drive, and let the counter climb. By the late game the total will be close; a final shopping run closes the gap. Keep the receipts in the stats screen.
trophies.tips: Spend as you play — gear for other trophies counts too; a final shopping run closes the gap.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Garage properties are the safehouses of the car collector, and this trophy wants every one of them bought. Properties appear on the map as you progress and earn money — buy each one as it becomes available rather than saving them for the end, because the later garages cost real money and the early ones are cheap. Owning them all also gives you somewhere to keep the rare vehicles the discovery trophy needs. When the last deed is signed, the trophy pops.
trophies.tips: Buy each garage as it appears — early ones are cheap, and they store the rare cars too.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: The Scooter Bros app is Leonida's vehicle registry, and this trophy wants ten vehicles registered on it. Registration is a small interaction: find a vehicle, open the app, and log it. Any ten count, so register the cars you actually drive — your daily driver, the mission vehicles, anything you spend time in. The app's list shows what is already registered, so there is no guessing. Ten registrations, done in an afternoon of normal driving, and the trophy pops.
trophies.tips: Register the cars you actually drive — the app lists what's already logged.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; Scooter Bros app
